what: Fix 1 — -9 sentinel not scrubbed by fix_types = TRUE (R/utilities.R)
title: icesDatras — Project Notes
text: fixed: applyDatrasTypeSchema() now replaces numeric -9 / -9L NA int decimal columns, type coercion. parseDatras() alone insufficient: parseDatras() scrubs -9 via string comparison (x[x == -9] <- NA), catches string "-9" "-9.0" — valid decimal representation DATRAS uses missing float fields. simplify() converts strings numeric, -9.0 value becomes -9 passes applyDatrasTypeSchema() unchanged. Upstream issue raise: > fix_types = TRUE fully scrub DATRAS -9 sentinels > > applyDatrasTypeSchema() coerces column types never converts -9 sentinel NA. > parseDatras() attempts via string comparison, misses decimal representations > "-9.0". Minimal reproducible example: > > r > # Simulate parseDatras + simplify produce "-9.0" decimal field: > x <- data.frame(HaulDur = -9)   # numeric -9 survived simplify() > applyDatrasTypeSchema(x, record = "HH")$HaulDur > #> [1] -9   # expected NA > > > Sentinel scrubbing applied inside applyDatrasTypeSchema() int decimal > columns, fix_types = TRUE reliable single-step clean-regardless values > arrive.

title: icesDatras — Project Notes

([^ >]+)[^>]* tag attributes skipped without relying > lazy quantifier support: > > r > gsub(" *<([^ >]+)[^>]*>.*", "\\1", '    <Age_6 xsi:nil="true">NA</Age_6>') > #> [1] "Age_6" >

what: Fix 4 — a numeric column stays character("NA") when it’s entirely missing in one
title: icesDatras — Project Notes
text: response, even Fix 3’s name fix (found obus side, 2026-07-21; applied 2026-07-22, einar_dev/age-na-string-coercion) Distinct Fix 3. Fix 3 stops xsi:nil attribute leaking column name. separate bug column’s value, one level deeper — happens even Fix 3 already applied, whenever every value numeric column missing given response (single-row response — getIndices()/getCPUEAge() — case likely trigger , since ’s row’s real value pull column’s inferred type toward numeric). Root cause, pieces R/utilities.R: parseDatras() line 46 turns self-closing/empty tag literal text "NA": Two lines later, -9 "" explicitly normalized real NA: "NA" string substitution just created never similarly normalized — survives genuine, non-missing character value way simplify(). simplify() decides whether character column can safely converted numeric comparing NA counts conversion: .numeric("NA") correctly yields NA_real_, sum(.na(y)) counts every row -missing column correctly. .na("NA") FALSE — character string "NA" real, present value .na()’s point view, missing one — sum(.na(x)) 0 column made entirely converted empty tags. 0 != n, guard fails, whole column left character, literal text "NA" every cell. Reproduce (pre-fix behaviour): Impact: affects every function going formatDatras(fix_types = TRUE) whenever numeric column entirely missing one response — getIndices()/getCPUEAge() especially, since return exactly one row per call. Building archive many separate per-call responses (normal usage pattern ) means files get column numeric others character, breaking tool expects one type per column across files (DuckDB, Arrow, bind_rows() without prior coercion) — exactly found, obus side, building per-response parquet archive getIndices() output. Fix applied: parseDatras(), self-closing-tag expansion now produces empty content instead literal text "NA" (first two options ), existing x[x == ""] <- NA normalisation catches — every column type, just numeric ones. Also confirmed live: declared-character columns (e.g. StatRec) identical gap now covered , just Age_*. Full writeup commit-pinned citations fork upstream: ~/R/Pakkar/obus/dev/upstream_reports/getindices_age_column_type_inconsistency.qmd.
code: x <- gsub("^ *<(.*?) />$", "<\\1> NA </\\1>", x) x[x == -9] <- NA x[x == ""] <- NA if (is.character(x)) {   y <- as.numeric(x)   if (sum(is.na(y)) == sum(is.na(x)))     x <- y } d <- getIndices(survey = "NS-IBTS", year = 1965, quarter = 1, species = 126417,                 fix_types = TRUE, new_names = TRUE) sapply(d[grep("^Age_", names(d))], class) # before the fix: Age_0-5 numeric/integer (real catch at those ages here); Age_6-15 # character, holding the literal string "NA". After the fix (verified live): all 16 # Age_0..Age_15 columns come back numeric/integer, none character.

what: 3. xsi:nil XML attribute leaking into column names
title: Recent Fixes and Field-List Corrections
text: DATRAS represents missing field self-closing tag, e.g. <Age_6 xsi:nil="true" />. parseDatras()’s name-extraction regex relied lazy quantifier ((.*?)) isn’t reliably supported across regex engines, captured whole Age_6 xsi:nil="true" column name instead Age_6. Fix: replaced ([^ >]+)[^>]*, stops capture first space > without relying lazy-quantifier support. Verified live: 16 Age_0-Age_15 columns real getIndices() call now come back clean names.

what: 4. Literal text "NA" surviving as a real, non-missing value
title: Recent Fixes and Field-List Corrections
text: deeper, separate bug area: self-closing-tag expansion parseDatras() produced literal text "NA" field’s content, true NA. Two lines later, -9 "" explicitly normalised NA – "NA" never included, .na("NA") FALSE, simplify()’s numeric-conversion guard fooled left whole column character, holding string "NA" every affected cell. Fix: tag expansion now produces empty content rather literal text "NA", existing x[x == ""] <- NA normalisation catches – every column type, just numeric ones. real gap beyond Age_*: declared-character columns got zero scrubbing either.
